outcome.product_goal: A user selects an authorized local folder in a native macOS application and Outis locally produces a separate tokenized Markdown repository while keeping sensitive mappings in a private local vault.
outcome.first_business_goal: Demonstrate the complete local workflow on synthetic data for fundraising conversations without representing the demo as production-ready, secure, anonymous, or perfectly detected.
outcome.controlled_pilot_goal: After the demo, measure extraction, detection, entity resolution, determinism, vault isolation, cancellation, and publication behavior before any approved confidential-data pilot.
outcome.agent_response_contract: Agents may return Outis tokens such as {{person.person_0001}}. Plaintext response rendering is outside the first pilot.

delivery_strategy.principle: Build the smallest complete vertical slice, then add one measured capability at a time.
fast_iteration_rules: Protocols and approval gates remain mandatory.
Every implementation item must bind to a pilot acceptance criterion or an active invariant.
Unsupported inputs must fail explicitly; they must not receive speculative handling.
No future-service scaffolding, generalized plugin system, or unused abstraction is permitted.
Each increment must preserve source, vault, staging, and agent-repository separation.
A completed job means processing finished under the declared contract; it does not mean every sensitive value was found.
Claims are limited to recorded evidence from the tested version, fixtures, machine, and configuration.
priority_order: plaintext exclusion from the agent repository under a declared oracle
deterministic replay under declared inputs and vault state
clear review, failure, cancellation, and publication behavior
measured extraction fidelity and platform convenience

recommended_first_slice.approval_status: S1-22C is explicitly approved and closes the normalized-document caller-limit contradiction. The amended author pre-audit and separate peer audit passed. The exact MI-02 implementation plan is explicitly approved; the clean committed baseline and repeated offline preflight remain required before code.
user_flow: Select an authorized source folder and a separate export destination.
Run one local job and observe progress.
Review every binary extraction and uncertain candidate using the exact minimal actions; unresolved or rejected extraction and identity conflicts remain blocked.
Publish only after extraction, review, vault, and staged-output validation succeeds.
Open the generated Markdown repository and use it as the only repository granted to the tested agent.

required_initial: scanned or image-only PDF through local OCR
source_formats.target_contract: Every successfully processed source produces one .md in a separate repository named outis. The output mirrors source-relative directories and base names after sensitive path-component tokenization and replaces the source extension with .md. A target collision blocks publication; nothing is overwritten or silently omitted.
source_formats.normalization_contract: Markdown and plain text preserve their BOM-free UTF-8 text. Binary-derived text uses the selected plain-text Markdown line/page normalization, carries private page or mode provenance, and is not represented as layout-faithful or complete.
source_formats.review_contract: Every .doc, .docx, native-text PDF, and OCR result requires local review of original plus normalized text. Confirmation binds exact source and normalized hashes without proving completeness; rejection blocks the job. Corrupt, encrypted, signature-mismatched, embedded, incomplete, unsupported, source-mutated, or out-of-bound input blocks explicitly.
source_formats.determinism_contract: Native extraction identity includes the source bytes, macOS product/build, framework environment, Vision revision and options, language-support result, 200-DPI render identity, observation ordering, and normalized-document schema. Cross-OS-build equality is not promised.
source_formats.evidence_status: S1 approves strict Rust UTF-8 decoding plus AppKit Word import, PDFKit PDF text and rendering, Core Graphics fixed rendering, and Vision revision 3 OCR. Every binary-format result requires review. These extraction and application surfaces remain unimplemented and require their later lifecycle gates.

human_languages.scope_status: Italian, German, and French are mandatory in the first slice.
human_languages.evidence_status: R1.1 provides a 30-case synthetic contextual-detection smoke corpus. R1.2 confirms Vision revision 3 exposes Italian, German, and French on the measured host and records a synthetic OCR probe. Repository-owned language and extraction oracles remain an S1/P1 requirement.

largely_language_independent: approved telephone syntax after explicit locale and normalization rules
token assignment, ordering, serialization, and publication
language_dependent: titles, abbreviations, aliases, morphology, and ambiguous words
deterministic_language_boundary.extension_rule: Core contracts must not hardcode one human language, but no additional language is called supported until its corpus and per-language oracles pass.
deterministic_language_boundary.performance_rule: The deterministic gate is expected to be lightweight, but its latency and throughput remain measured budgets rather than assumed claims.

deferred_until_policy_and_oracles_exist: credentials and secrets beyond explicitly declared structured patterns

discovery_layers.behavior: Deterministic, class-specific detectors and normalization for approved structured classes.

R1.1 selected one exact on-device mBERT ONNX candidate for person and organization spans and location-component evidence. It does not emit complete postal addresses; model output remains untrusted candidate evidence.
Exact normalized matches are linked across documents; uncertain alias or entity merges require review rather than hidden heuristics.
Uncertain, conflicting, incomplete, unsupported, or corrupt content receives needs_review or blocked and cannot be silently published as complete.

model_policy.pilot_requirement: The first slice requires exactly one approved offline multilingual NER detector for contextual person and organization candidates and location-component evidence for deterministic postal-address assembly.
model_policy.initial_direction: Evaluate and select an existing fixed on-device NER model before considering training or fine-tuning.
model_policy.model_selection: S1 approves Davlan/bert-base-multilingual-cased-ner-hrl revision e756de7f7b8f64fea0c3d7c3872f1322fab747b1 with its publisher ONNX artifact and ONNX Runtime 1.28.0 CPU execution for the first-slice design. Qualified legal clearance blocks only model-specific implementation, acquisition, packaging, execution, distribution, and complete-pilot acceptance.

execution.session_lifetime: one immutable session per active job; release at terminal job status
execution.configuration_policy: fixed first-slice configuration; no user thread selector or automatic tuning

minimal_structure.rust: The complete pilot has exactly three Rust crates: dependency-light outis-core, side-effecting outis-runtime, and the outis-ffi boundary. MI-01 created the current one-member outis-core workspace; no empty runtime or FFI placeholder is allowed.
minimal_structure.swift: S1-11 approves exactly one native macOS application target and one test target for the first slice. Do not create a Finder extension target until a future specification approves it.
minimal_structure.ffi: S1-12 approves exactly ten version-one C ABI functions, opaque handles, pointer-length buffers, stable call codes, polling, extraction and review submission, cancellation races, panic containment, explicit release, cbindgen 0.29.4, and byte-clean generated-header verification.
minimal_structure.tests: Keep synthetic fixtures, evaluation tools, and benchmarks outside production targets.

stop_or_replan_conditions: No acceptable local detector can be evaluated for the declared Italian, German, and French classes.
The selected runtime cannot satisfy local-only, licensing, artifact-identity, application-size, or memory constraints.
The tested agent cannot be prevented from reading the source or private vault under the declared threat model.
Extraction completeness or offset provenance cannot be specified for an allegedly supported format.
The vault and secret boundary cannot provide the required transaction, recovery, and denied-caller behavior.
Rust-to-Swift ownership, cancellation, error, and build behavior cannot be made explicit and testable.
A proposed shortcut would publish uncertain or partial content as complete.
Fundraising timing pressure would require claims beyond measured evidence.
current_blockers_to_code: MI-01 is complete; no additional code is authorized by its closed plan.

S1-22 through S1-22C are approved, and the amended MI-02 author pre-audit and separate peer audit passed. The exact MI-02 implementation plan exists and still requires explicit approval, a clean committed baseline, and repeated offline preflight.

S1-22A corrects the exhaustive SensitiveClassV1 compatibility claim, S1-22B defines one maximal telephone-extension digit run with exact 1-through-6 and 7-or-more classification, and S1-22C establishes the Section 8 10 MiB caller ceiling.
Repository-owned extraction and OCR fixtures and their complete oracles do not exist; this blocks extraction and complete-pilot work, not the proposed pure MI-02 detector increment.

The selected model still requires legal review, but this blocks only its dependencies, source, tests, fixtures, acquisition, integration, execution, packaging, distribution, and complete-pilot acceptance.
The plaintext funding-demo vault is restricted to synthetic data and is not an approved confidential-data design.
Xcode 26.6, SDK 26.5, Swift 6.3.3, macOS 26.5, and disposable arm64 Swift-to-Rust linkage are verified; the complete Outis application build remains unproved until implementation.
No manifest, dependency, build, Swift, Xcode, runtime, FFI, model, vault, tokenization, or publication change is authorized by S1-22.
